cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: The UK produces approximately 9.5 million tonnes of food waste per year; about 70% of this was intended for human consumption and could have been eaten.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: Food waste occurs at every stage: production (crops left in fields), processing (trimming, quality rejection), retail (overstocking, past display dates), and consumer (over-buying, cooking too much, not using leftovers).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: Households produce the most food waste (around 70% of the UK total), mainly from buying too much, not using food before it spoils, and cooking larger portions than needed.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: When food waste goes to landfill, it decomposes anaerobically, producing methane — a greenhouse gas 25 times more potent than carbon dioxide.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: WRAP (Waste and Resources Action Programme) runs the Love Food Hate Waste campaign to help consumers reduce household food waste.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: Strategies to reduce food waste: meal planning, writing shopping lists, correct portion sizes, using leftovers creatively, understanding date labels, and proper storage.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: Retailers reduce waste through: dynamic pricing (marking down near-date food), donating surplus to charities (e.g. FareShare), and improving demand forecasting.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: Nose-to-tail and root-to-stem eating use all parts of an animal or plant, reducing waste from butchery and vegetable preparation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: Composting converts food waste into nutrient-rich soil conditioner, diverting it from landfill and reducing methane emissions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Waste & Sustainability
cards.back: Anaerobic digestion of food waste produces biogas (for energy) and digestate (for fertiliser), turning waste into a resource.

cards.front: What should you know about food preparation & nutrition exam tips — food waste & sustainability?
cards.back: 1. For Food Waste & Sustainability questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2. Check your answer makes sense in context (estimation, units, reasonableness) 3. Use correct mathematical notation and state formulae before substituting values 4. If a Food Waste & Sustainability question asks you to 'prove' or 'show', write a logical chain of reasoning with a conclusion line 5. For problem-solving, identify the topic first, then recall the relevant method
